newsitem.title: GERMANY: German unemployment falls in March - sources.
newsitem.headline: German unemployment falls in March - sources.

text.p: German unemployment fell in March to 4.48 million, down 190,000 from February's 64-year record of 4.67 million, sources who had gained access to data from the Federal Labour Office told Reuters on Monday.
The number of people out of work, based on unadjusted data, fell in both the richer western part of Germany and in the formerly communist east, the sources added.
The Labour Office is due to release official jobless data on Tuesday.
Despite the month-on-month fall, unadjusted unemployment was still around 340,000 higher than in March 1996.

The sources said unemployment in western Germany had fallen in March to around 3.13 million from 3.257 million in February. In eastern Germany, the jobless total was around 1.35 million, down from 1.414 million in the previous month.

Unadjusted unemployment is the most politically sensitive jobs number in Germany, and has a direct impact on the country's ability to rein in borrowing this year to qualify for Europe's single currency.
The sources gave no figures for seasonally-adjusted joblessness -- the figure watched more closely by independent economists to assess the underlying trend in the German jobs market.
